newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian police killing triggers riot in St. Marc.
newsitem.headline: Haitian police killing triggers riot in St. Marc.

text.p: Haitian National Police in the northern city of St. Marc restored order on Monday after demonstrators blocked roads and burned a police station following the fatal police shooting on Saturday of a civilian.
Police reinforcements from Gonaives were sent to St. Marc on Monday in case further violence erupted, officials said.
The weekend demonstrators told Haitian radio stations they thought police were acting with impunity in St. Marc, and drastic measures were necessary.
"The police cannot do what they want," said one demonstrator, angry that a local citizen had been shot at his home by a police agent.
The victim was identified as Legros Mecellus but the name of the officer was not immediately available on Monday from U.N. or police sources, who characterised the shooting as a mistake.

Police officers reported being threatened by angry mobs on Sunday. "They confiscated my gun, they told me to lay on the ground. One had a machete, one had a cord to tie me up. Another had gasoline to burn the police car ... after one hit me a few times, they let me go," said one officer who asked not to be identified..

Public Security Minister Robert Manuel said on Monday some 500 new recruits would be trained to strengthen the national police force before U.N. troops are scheduled to depart July 30. There are currently 5,000 Haitian police officers, with about half of them working in the capital.

About 1,200 U.N. troops still patrol Haiti's streets, mostly in Port-au-Prince. They took over security responsibilities from 20,000 U.S. troops who restored President Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power in October 1994, three years after he was ousted in a bloody military coup.
